title: Stops
summary: Every stop's own life, apart from the service plans, and the work asked for at the stops, each job on a screen of its own: the stops on a map beside their list or as a table, the stops nearest you in the field, one stop's page (its record under headings, its changes as a card), a site survey as one page of the worksheet's sections, a request's page from draft to its work order and completion, the work across every stop as a table, and what the feed changed.
questions: Where is each stop, and where does it stand on a given day: planned, permitted, built, in service, suspended, or retired?
Which stops are nearest me, here in the field?
Which stops are out of service on a day, since when, until when, and why?
What is at a stop — shelter, bench, lighting, a schedule — and can a wheelchair user board there?
Which routes stop here in the schedule running that day?
What has happened to this stop, and when?
Record a change: a new stop, its next stage, a suspension and its return, a move, new details, or a correction.
What did the last site survey find at this stop, and who surveyed it?
What work has been requested at this stop, and where is its work order?
What work is in flight across every stop, and where?
What did the agency's feed change in the stops record, and which stops in service does it not list?
session: 2026-11-13 on C-TRAN (testdata/ctran-gtfs.zip, `just qa`), at 2560x1300 and 390x844, after the full-width rebuild: stop 1132 found by typing its name and opened as a page; suspended from the change card; surveyed on the survey page (a section reached from the index, an amenity set, saved with a photo); a repair request made on its page, submitted, its work order opened through the stub, its utility locate edited in place; the Work table and Feed review; the stops' map kept across two trips to a stop and back (no map rebuilt), each stop's map opened at the stop; the stops as a table; on the phone, Nearby stops from the device's location, the stop page, the survey full screen, a field report saved as a draft, and the details card. Found and fixed before it: every job squeezed into one side panel (the survey a nine-step wizard with unnamed steps), conversational headings, the stops' map rebuilt and the stop's map flying in on each visit.
